newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Oct housing completions fell 0.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Oct housing completions fell 0.7 pct.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Department report on completions of new privately-owned housing units, seasonally adjusted annual rates, in 1,000s, with percent changes from prior months and year over year.
Housing completions by region, seasonally adj., in 1,000s:

Completions of single-family homes were unchanged in October after September was revised to a 3.4 percent drop, and August revised to a 0.5 percent increase. Previously, the department said single-family completions fell 4.2 percent in September and rose 0.7 percent in August.

October multi-family unit completions fell 3.5 percent after a revised 12.6 percent drop in September and a revised 2.6 percent decrease in August. Previously, the department said September multi-family unit completions fell 12.5 percent and that August multi-family unit completions were off 4.3 percent.

The department said actual completions on an unadjusted basis rose in October to 129,400 units from 121,200 units in September but were off from 134,100 units in August. In October last year, actual completions were reported at 125,400.

Privately-owned housing units under construction fell to a seasonally adjusted 828,000 in October from 829,000 in September but were up from 820,000 in August. They compare with 781,000 units under construction in October last year.
